newsitem.title: USA: CBOT July soybeans touch limit on tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: CBOT July soybeans touch limit on tight supplies.

text.p: Concerns about the availability of soybeans for spot shipment caused July soybeans to briefly rally to the 30-cent daily trading limit Friday, traders said.
Importers of U.S. soybeans expressed concerns about low U.S. soybean stocks following supply and demand forecasts from the U.S. Department of Agriculture on Thursday.
"The overall soybean ending stocks for the 1996/97 (Sept/Aug) are still relatively too low," said a Taiwanese soybean buyer.
USDA raised its stocks forecast by five million bushels, but supplies were still hovering near 20-year lows.
July also plowed through several key technical levels. That activity triggered heavy buy-stop orders and accelerated the pace of gains, traders said.
July pushed through the 50-day moving average at $8.55-1/2 cents a bushel and last year's high of $8.56.
In early trade, Refco and Rosenthal Collins each bought two million bushels July and ADM bought one million July, traders said.
At 1111 CDT July soybeans were 23 cents a bushel higher at $8.65, and other months were four to 13-1/4 higher.
